how_customers_find_and_choose: Parents and students choose from word of mouth, reviews and the map listing, then visit or message the institution
Parents look for teacher quality, safety, results and how quickly the school or centre replies to a question
Short videos from classes, events and student work show what the place feels like
Adults choosing skills courses compare outcomes, schedule and format, and often ask in chat before enrolling
Online and hybrid classes are an accepted option, especially for languages, tests and skills
what_works_now: A clear course or class outline with timings, who teaches and what the student will be able to do
A quick reply to enquiries with a visit, trial class or demo offered
Parent communication in chat or short notes: attendance, homework, progress, fee reminders
Student work, performances and events shown with the permission of families
Collecting honest feedback from parents or students each term and acting on it
A simple enrolment and fee follow-up routine with polite written reminders
Alumni or past student stories shared with permission
outdated_or_weak: Printed pamphlets and wall banners as the main source of admissions
Making unverifiable promises about results, jobs or admissions
Sharing photos of children without family permission
Advice to 'go viral' with no content the school can actually produce
Fee reminders by shouting at parents at pickup or by public lists

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Admission cycles follow the academic calendar; Ramadan and summer breaks shift timetables
Parents often pay fees monthly or termly in cash or by bank transfer
Schools and institutes are registered with the education authority; the owner confirms specifics with it
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Schools follow different curricula and are regulated by the education authority; parents compare them on curriculum, fees and ratings
Many students and parents are expatriates choosing by curriculum and location
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Education and childcare providers are licensed and regulated by province; the owner confirms specifics
International students are a large audience for colleges and consultants

never_assume: A website with an enrolment form
Permission from families to share photos
A tracked list of enquiries and follow-ups
